info.name: PatTokenApi
info.description:
GraphQL API test suite dedicated to the Personal Access Token (PAT) feature (Sdl\imtauth\1.0\PersonalAccessTokens.sdl): CreateToken, GetToken, GetTokenList, ValidateToken, RevokeToken, DeleteToken. Covers input validation, error-envelope shape, idempotency, ownership (or lack thereof), and - as the centerpiece - the scope ∩ actual-user-permission intersection enforced by CAuthenticationManagerComp::CreateGqlContext for PAT-authenticated GraphQL requests, probed via GetUserPermissions (Sdl\imtauth\1.0\Permissions.sdl).

Built by analogy with ProLife's own ProLifeApiPostman and DeskTicketApiPostman (collection-level apikey auth header x-authentication-token, global pre-request/test scripts, numbered phase folders, bootstrap-creates-its-own-users). Does NOT modify or duplicate Tests\backend\postman_collection.json's existing PersonalAccessTokens folder (legacy, happy-path only, git-tracked) - this is a new, standalone, more complete suite.

Folder 09 covers the productId cross-product storage (same user, multiple products, one central Puma store). Folder 10 asserts that omitting the now-non-null (`!` in SDL) `input` argument is rejected at dispatch with 'Bad request. Unexpected request for command-ID' before the resolver (it used to be opt-in folder 90, informational-only, because omitted input reached the resolver and tripped a Debug Q_ASSERT). Folder 11 proves PATs are safe across products: the token's own productId tag is not an authorization boundary (a token minted for one product still authenticates against a request scoped to a different product, source-confirmed via CAuthenticationManagerComp::CreateGqlContext, which keys permission lookup off the productid HTTP header, never the token's stored productId), but no permissions leak across the mismatch (CUserBaseInfo::GetPermissions(productId) is a per-product map lookup, empty for an unconfigured product), and RevokeToken/DeleteToken for one product's token never affects another product's token for the same user. Folder 91 remains opt-in - it requires a real 5-minute wait to observe the auth-cache TTL boundary and is excluded from the default Newman --folder list (see README).
